draft_paragraphs.uq_axes_and_calibration: We distinguish four aspects of probabilistic performance: point accuracy, marginal calibration, sharpness, and joint dependence. Log-scale point error measures central prediction accuracy; empirical interval coverage and interval width describe calibration and sharpness; CRPS jointly evaluates the location and spread of marginal predictive distributions; and joint log density and the variogram score probe dependence across target coordinates [Tran2020, Busk2022]. Improvement in one quantity need not improve the others. In particular, the Student-t diagnostic tests whether observation-dependent scale can reduce local undercoverage, but its wider intervals and worse one-sided CRPS prevent treating it as an adopted calibration repair [ThomasMitchell2023]. A distributional change is not independent calibration. Any subsequent conformal layer would require prespecified, unconsumed calibration units and assumptions linking them to deployment; pointwise or cellwise coverage must not be presented as simultaneous curve coverage [Gopakumar2026].
draft_paragraphs.evidence_roles: The evidence has four distinct roles. Numerical verification checks whether the implementation reproduces the stated Gaussian calculations and information-access rules; it does not establish material validity. Formulation-level leave-one-out evaluation of the 25 development formulations describes retrospective performance in a dataset already used during method development. The 46 source-inspected external curves provide a no-retraining transfer stress test under changes in chemistry, material state, and acquisition, rather than blinded confirmation of independent preparation-batch generalization. A future same-domain confirmation would freeze the method, anchor rule, comparison methods, endpoints, and material grouping before accessing new target curves [Jakeman2025v2]. These distinctions prevent repeated coordinates, masks, numerical checks, or reused outcomes from being counted as additional independent material evidence.
